html:
Kuyam is the name the map gives to the Chumash people of the Cuyama Valley, an inland valley in the mountains of central California, east of today's Santa Maria. The Cuyama River and valley take their name from a Chumash village called Kuyam.

The inland Chumash here hunted, gathered acorns and seeds, and traded both with the coast and with the Yokuts of the San Joaquin Valley. From the late 1700s they were drawn into the Spanish missions of the region, and their villages emptied. Little else is recorded about them as a separate group.
